description: PWA dashboard for monitoring OpenWrt/GL.iNet home networks: fleet status, per-router health, devices, WireGuard peers, AdGuard Home stats and alerts in real time (SSE). Go backend + React 19 frontend, SQLite, multi-user, i18n

latest_release.body:
# NetPulse 2.54.0

This release is about what the screen was not telling you. Four features make the panel explain more, and a batch of fixes make it stop lying in the places where it was.

## Icons that name the device

![Searching the icon picker by the word Fridge and the row taking the new icon](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gnacho/netpulse/v2.54.0/docs/releases/2.54.0/icon-picker.gif)

Sixty smart-home icons in ten categories, searchable by their name in your language. A fridge stops looking like a generic box, and the search finds it by typing what it is. The catalog came from @Bann-DEV in #2107, and #2113 is the test that keeps it honest when someone adds a tile.

## What each device asks for

![DNS activity for one device with the 1 hour and 24 hour windows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gnacho/netpulse/v2.54.0/docs/releases/2.54.0/dns-activity.gif)

Per-device DNS activity from the AdGuard query log: the domains a client resolves, how often, and which ones were blocked, in a one hour or one day window. It sits in the device detail, next to the client that asked. #2081 built it, and #2119 made it show something, because it was reading with a lower case MAC while the log was stored in upper case.

## Quiet is not offline

![A neighbour entry in STALE coming back to REACHABLE and the host staying online](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gnacho/netpulse/v2.54.0/docs/releases/2.54.0/presence.gif)

A wired host with a static address that goes quiet used to drop off the map. Now the unit pings its stale neighbour and re-reads the table, so the address and the MAC are confirmed and an idle host stays online. #2108 added the recheck, #2109 extended it to IPv6 over NDP, and #2110 sweeps the subnets a unit routes to find hosts that never left an entry at all. The report behind it is #2063.

## Chinese and Russian

![The same panel in English, Spanish, Chinese and Russian, with dates following each language](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gnacho/netpulse/v2.54.0/docs/releases/2.54.0/languages.gif)

The whole interface in Chinese and in Russian, catalogs complete and reviewed. Dates and numbers follow each language too, not only the labels. Chinese came in #2070, from @Bann-DEV, and Russian in #2083, from @sers88.

## Also in this release

- **What's new page.** The app now explains each release with animated cards, in all four languages. #2116 added it, and the dot on the version stamp stays until you open it.
- **Traffic per client.** The device detail shows down, up and total over 1 hour, 24 hours, 30 days and 12 months, with the series for the same window. @tombacchetta asked for it in #2076 and the panel answers with the per-client history the server already had.
- **Wi-Fi clients with no IP** are marked as such, and leave one info entry in the activity log after two minutes instead of looking broken. #2111 closed the request @crowedavid opened in #1984.
- **Docker.** An optional server image with the UI and the agents inside, published to GHCR on every tag for amd64 and arm64. @sers88 wrote it in #2101 and the pipeline in #2105.
- **A smaller agent.** Built without `encoding/json/v2`: 7.8 MB down to 7.4 MB on amd64, which is 5.8% less. #2096 measured it before and after.
- **The client table** rebalances its columns and uses a single line in the 2xl tier, from #2106.
- **A quieter panel.** The SNMP community field says it is read-only (#2080), the unit column is translated (#2098), the splash background follows the theme (#2099) and the landing page counts demo clicks (#2093).

## Fixed

- The per-device DNS panel showed nothing until #2119 fixed the case mismatch between what ingest stored and what the request asked for.
- Responses from handlers that wait on a unit died at the 15 second write timeout, so a reinstall that worked still showed a red "server unreachable" line. #2112 gave each handler its own ceiling, and it came from the install report in #1894.
- The rack offers cables between fleet units again, f

Make device name sources explicit and configurable

You know these communities better than I do: where should NetPulse be told about?
Time to change your stars request. :)
Router integration policy: OpenWrt and SNMP in core, external agents for everything else
Should containers (Docker/LXC/k8s) be a first-class device type?
Proposal: Extensible router integrations through a plugin architecture

# NetPulse

English | Español

The pulse of your home network. Real time. No cloud.
Watch your routers, draw your topology, score your network's health and get alerted, from a single self-hosted binary. Nothing ever leaves your LAN.

Try the live demo · Full feature tour

## See it before you install it You don't need a single router to see NetPulse working: - **[demo.netpulse.cloudless.club](https://demo.netpulse.cloudless.club)** is the real app with a full sample network loaded, read-only, no sign-up. Click around, change the theme, switch languages, watch the live updates. - **[netpulse.cloudless.club/features](https://netpulse.cloudless.club/features)** is the complete feature inventory: every screen and feature, with the technical decisions and the honest scope of each one. ## What you get **Fleet overview and a health score that means something.** One 0-100 score condenses latency, loss, uptime and temperature per router and for the whole network, updated live every 5 seconds over SSE. Live WAN traffic against your contracted plan, alert feed, AdGuard Home stats and WireGuard peers on the same screen (that's the screenshot above). **A topology map that draws itself.** Inferred live from the bridge FDB (and LLDP where available, including LLDP-MIB on SNMP-managed switches): wired and wireless clients under the router and port they actually talk through, managed and inferred switches, Proxmox hosts with their VMs nested, and WireGuard tunnels drawn from peer to Internet. Quiet devices keep their place; nothing jumps around on refresh. Drag nodes to arrange it and the layout stays yours.

**Every device, classified.** Hostnames, IPs, type detection (hostname patterns + OUI), first seen, band and signal for Wi-Fi clients, and the router each one is attached to. A static host that nothing else names, typically a switch or a server that never takes a DHCP lease, still gets its name from a forward-confirmed reverse lookup, done in the background and only for private addresses. Label devices, reserve IPs, and see when something new shows up.

**Per-router health at a glance.** Model, firmware, CPU, memory, temperature, uptime and live traffic for each router, with port-level history and per-band client splits. SNMP-polled managed switches are first-class citizens too, and any unit can be paused without removing it: no polling, no alerts, history kept.

**WAN speed tests, on demand or on a schedule.** Run a test from the server whenever you need one, or schedule it by interval, weekly, monthly, or during the quietest hour based on the previous seven days of traffic. Results stay in SQLite with a seven-day chart and recent history. Choose M-Lab NDT (the default), Ookla, Cloudflare, LibreSpeed or a custom HTTP endpoint, and get an alert when download speed falls below your chosen percentage of the contracted plan. **What it runs on.** The server is one static Go binary on any Linux box. The agent is what talks to your routers, and how it gets there depends on the platform: | Platform | How the agent runs | Notes | |---|---|---| | OpenWrt (incl. GL.iNet) | Native `netpulse-agent` package (`.ipk`/`.apk`) | procd, UCI config, `luci-app-netpulse`, in-app install and upgrade | | MikroTik (RouterOS) | External `routeros-pusher` in [netpulse-integrations](https://github.com/gnacho/netpulse-integrations/tree/main/routeros) | Read-only over the binary API (REST fallback): system, ports, DHCP, ARP, FDB, temperature, firmware and WAN traffic. Deployed and managed from the Integrations section | | Asuswrt / Asuswrt-Merlin | External `asuswrt-pusher` in [netpulse-integrations](https://github.com/gnacho/netpulse-integrations/tree/main/asuswrt) | Static binary under `/jffs/netpulse` (Merlin layout), using `/proc`, `iw` and `lldpd`. Deployed over SSH from the Integrations section, key or password sign-in | | OPNsense (firewall) | External `opnsense-pusher` in [netpulse-integrations](https://github.com/gnacho/netpulse-integrations/tree/main/opnsense) | Read-only API key with minimum privileges: system, interface counters, IPv4 ARP, WAN rates with an explicitly selected interface, memory and temperature. Beta | | UniFi (self-hosted controller) | External `unifi-pusher` in [netpulse-integrations](https://github.com/gnacho/netpulse-integrations/tree/main/unifi) | Read-only, one site: gateways, switches and APs with ports and uplinks, clients with band and signal, gateway uptime. Deployed from the Integrations section | | External router families | Separate Go pusher in [netpulse-integrations](https://github.com/gnacho/netpulse-integrations) | See the [external integrations guide](docs/external-integrations.md) | | Managed switches | SNMP | Port states, speeds and LLDP-MIB neighbours | | Realtek switches (RTL8372/8373) | Embedded beacon in the [RTLPlayground fork](https://github.com/gnacho/RTLPlayground) | Port state, byte rates and FDB over UDP. Advanced firmware setup, see the [Realtek switch beacon guide](docs/RTL-SWITCH-BEACON.md) | Vendor integrations live outside the server on purpose. An OpenWrt router never carries code for RouterOS, Bbox or another platform, and each integration can be tested and released on its own schedule. Whoever owns the hardware validates it, while NetPulse maintains only the shared ingest contract. **And the rest of the tour:** - **WireGuard**: peers with real names, latest handshakes, transfer per peer and the traffic of the last 30 days, built from persisted per-peer counters because the counters WireGuard exposes restart at zero with every peer. - **AdGuard Home**: query stats, blocked share, top blocked domains. - **Wi-Fi and roaming**: signal matrix per AP, 802.11r status, channel utilization, persistent roaming events. - **Wi-Fi channel analyzer**: a real spectrum per radio, every network drawn on the frequency axis with a congestion score for every channel. It reads the air and advises; it never writes to your routers. - **Fleet firmware upgrades**: upgrade OpenWrt devices from the UI, vanilla OpenWrt only (device list filtered, with an explanatory note). - **Physical rack (Labs preview)**: draw your 19" rack, place your hardware and let NetPulse propose the cabling from the detected topology. Off by default. - **Alerts that find you**: temperature, new device, firmware available, WAN down, agent issues; bell feed plus notification channels (native Web Push, ntfy, Telegram and outgoing webhook). Notification channels only carry alerts marked as urgent; the feed level (none / urgent / all) is configured separately in Alerts. - **Multi-user**: bcrypt passwords, admin and viewer roles, per-user language (ES/EN/ZH/RU). - **Installable PWA**: phone or desktop, live over SSE, light/dark themes. - **A good OpenWrt citizen**: native `netpulse-agent` packages (`.ipk`/`.apk`), a `luci-app-netpulse` page, UCI config, procd init with self-heal. Or run the whole server on-box. - **Self-updating**: the built-in updater checks for releases and applies them with an atomic swap. - **MQTT + Home Assistant (opt-in)**: publish the fleet state (health, clients, per-router vitals and alerts) to an MQTT broker; Home Assistant discovers the entities on its own. Routers that expose themselves with NetGrip are not duplicated. Off by default and cloud-free: configured from the MQTT card in Settings (or with the `NETPULSE_MQTT_*` environment variables, or the equivalent `mqtt_*` UCI options on-box). Topics, entities and limits in the [manual](docs/manual.en.md#home-assistant-mqtt). **An MCP server for your AI assistant.** NetPulse embeds a read-only [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server (streamable HTTP at `/mcp`) so your assistant can query fleet status, per-router health, known devices, WireGuard peers, AdGuard Home stats, the topology graph and active alerts with an API token. Token-only auth (never the session cookie), rate limited, every call logged for audit. Disabled by default: enable it with `NETPULSE_MCP_ENABLED=1` and mint a token in Settings → API tokens. Keep the port on your LAN: anyone with the token can read your whole network state. That is still a selection: **[every feature is on the website](https://netpulse.cloudless.club/features)**, one by one, and everything above is clickable in the **[live demo](https://demo.netpulse.cloudless.club)**. ## Get started in about five minutes You need a Linux box with systemd (x86_64, arm64 or armv7; a small LXC or VM is plenty) and OpenWrt/GL.iNet routers on your LAN. MikroTik, Asuswrt/Merlin, OPNsense and UniFi controllers are supported through app-managed integrations, and anything with SSH or SNMP can be added by hand (see the folded section below). **1. Install the server** on the box: ```bash curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o /tmp/netpulse-install.sh https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gnacho/netpulse/main/install.sh && sh /tmp/netpulse-install.sh ``` The installer is plain, readable shell ([inspect it first](install.sh)): it detects distro and arch, downloads the release verified against `checksums.txt`, sets up a sandboxed `netpulse` systemd service and prints the initial admin password once. Re-running the same line updates; `sh install.sh --uninstall` removes. **2. Open the app** at `http://:3000`, log in with the printed password and the gateway is already there: NetPulse finds it on first boot via LAN discovery (a TCP :22 sweep with ubus/GL-UI fingerprinting). **3. Authorize the SSH key.** The server generated its own keypair on first boot. Copy the public key from **Settings → Fleet** and, on each router you want to monitor, append it: ```sh echo "" >> /etc/dropbear/authorized_keys ``` **4. Install the agents from the app.** Open **Routers** and scroll to the agents table: every OpenWrt router gets a row, and routers without an agent offer an **Install agent** button. One click and the server registers the agent, pushes the right binary for the router's architecture, writes the config and starts the service; it shows up as connected within seconds. Routers the server cannot SSH into use the pairing token instead (**Settings → Agent adoption**, see the folded section below). Asuswrt/Merlin, MikroTik, OPNsense and UniFi controllers use the vendor pushers from the Integrations section instead. **5. Take it with you.** Install the PWA from your browser (Add to home screen / Install app) and enable Web Push in Settings: alerts reach your phone even with the tab closed. Prefer to see it on your own hardware first? `DEMO_MODE=1 AUTH_PASS=choose-one ./netpulse` runs the same app with a 67-device sample network, no routers needed. `AUTH_PASS` is required even in demo mode: it protects the web session.
Other install paths **OpenWrt packages.** Every release ships `netpulse-agent` and `luci-app-netpulse` as installable packages (`.ipk` for OpenWrt 24.10, `.apk` for 25.12, plus x86/64). Grab them from the [latest release](https://github.com/gnacho/netpulse/releases): ```sh # OpenWrt 24.10 (ipk) opkg install ./netpulse-agent_*.ipk ./luci-app-netpulse_*.ipk # OpenWrt 25.12 (apk) apk add --allow-untrusted ./netpulse-agent-*.apk ./luci-app-netpulse-*.apk ``` The package ships an empty config, so point it at your server before starting: ```sh uci set netpulse-agent.main.server='http://:3000' uci set netpulse-agent.main.slug='' uci set netpulse-agent.main.token='<64-hex token>' uci commit netpulse-agent service netpulse-agent enable && service netpulse-agent start ``` If the server can already SSH into the router, skip all of this and press **Install agent** in the app: it does every step for you. **Pairing token.** For routers the server cannot reach over SSH, Settings → Agent adoption shows a reusable pairing token: `install-agent.sh --pairing-token` (run from any machine that can reach both the router and the server) registers the agent on first contact. **Asuswrt / Merlin.** Support lives in the external [`asuswrt-pusher`](https://github.com/gnacho/netpulse-integrations/tree/main/asuswrt) integration. Build its static binary, create the router as type `external` and copy the binary and environment file to `/jffs/`, which survives firmware updates. The integration README covers boot startup and manual upgrades. The pusher uses the portable probes for system data, wireless, DHCP, bridge FDB, ARP and LLDP. Features that require `ubus` or GL.iNet services remain absent, and the native agent upgrade and reinstall actions are not available. From the Integrations section the app can also install the pusher for you over SSH. An authorized server key is still the preferred path; when the router only accepts passwords, like the dropbear of a stock Asuswrt, set the password in the form and the server signs in with it. The password is stored in a 0600 companion file next to the integration environment file, never in the database, and a wrong password reports `ssh_auth_failed` instead of a generic SSH failure. **Latency sidecar.** Optional long-term TCP latency probes per router: ```bash curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o /tmp/netpulse-install-collector.sh https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gnacho/netpulse/main/install-collector.sh && sh /tmp/netpulse-install-collector.sh ``` Each probe is a TCP connection to the router that is closed without authenticating, so a router with dropbear logs it as `Child connection` followed by `Exit before auth: Exited normally`. That is the probe, not a failed login. `PROBE_PORT` (default `22`) points it at a listener that does not log every connection, for example the router's web UI on `80`, and `PROBE_INTERVAL` (default `5s`) sets how often it runs. **Docker.** If you prefer containers over systemd, a server image with the embedded UI and agent binaries is published on every release: ```bash docker run -d --name netpulse -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 -e AUTH_PASS=choose-one \ -v netpulse-data:/data --restart unless-stopped ghcr.io/gnacho/netpulse:latest ``` `AUTH_PASS` is required at boot (10+ characters); the port above is published on loopback — publish on a LAN interface instead if you want the panel reachable from other machines. Updates are `docker pull` + recreate; leave the in-app updater alone in this mode. Full guide: [docs/docker.md](docs/docker.md). **On-box mode.** No spare box? The server itself runs on an OpenWrt router, with UCI config and self-signed TLS with SPKI pinning.
## Updates and version history Releases are signed, checksummed and pushed to your fleet by the built-in auto-updater; the app shows a short human-readable "what changed" panel before you update. The full version history lives in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) and on the [releases page](https://github.com/gnacho/netpulse/releases); the plan ahead is in [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md). ## Documentation - **[User manual](docs/manual.en.md)** (also in [Spanish](docs/manual.es.md)): every screen explained, menu by menu, with step-by-step procedures. - **[Docker](docs/docker.md)**: optional container install path for the server, with compose and GHCR images. - **[Website](https://netpulse.cloudless.club)**: the project in five minutes, with a [feature tour](https://netpulse.cloudless.club/features), FAQ and screenshots. - **[Translations](docs/translations.md)**: how to add a language to the landing or to the panel, and what we check before merging it. - **[Roadmap](docs/ROADMAP.md)**: what's done, what's next. - **[Discussions](https://github.com/gnacho/netpulse/discussions)**: questions, ideas and shape-the-future talk. ## Big thanks NetPulse wouldn't exist without [OpenWrt](https://openwrt.org/). The whole premise of the project, that you can own and control your network hardware instead of depending on a vendor's closed firmware, only works because OpenWrt exists. If NetPulse is useful to you, the real credit goes to the OpenWrt community. This project is also shaped by its community: every issue, pull request and real-hardware test makes it better. Thanks to everyone who has contributed so far - the people and the work behind each release are named in the [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md) and in every release's notes. If you want to send code, read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) first: every PR runs the full build and test suite, and new server code lives in its own file with its test. ## Star history [![Star History Chart](https://api.star-history.com/svg?repos=gnacho/netpulse&type=date)](https://www.star-history.com/#gnacho/netpulse&date) ## License [AGPL-3.0](LICENSE)
